reason: The shared catalogue of controls, overlays, icons and output-card frames is kept as one library of typed partials: a Go parameter struct with validation, a named template and a stylesheet per part. Changed: overlays use the native dialog and popover elements, the Markdown, highlighting, diff and terminal renderers move to the host under area C4 and the library specifications, and labels are message keys or data by type instead of required props.

The three token tiers, the light, dark or system choice, the three font sizes and font lists, the icon sprite and theme registration are kept. Changed: one plain stylesheet in cascade layers with both schemes in one light-dark value, the scheme as an attribute the host renders with no boot script, appearance stored per principal as a host preference, and themes registered by compiled-in components with validation.

The script that solves three column widths is replaced by one CSS grid on the page shell's landmarks that states the same rule (the side panel concedes before the centre, which keeps 400 px). The ctx.layout service has no counterpart: navigation is the URL and widths are host preferences. The theme presenter is replaced by the attribute and generated stylesheet of the theme component, and the desktop window-chrome seats are not built because there is no desktop application.

The general docking engine (recursive split tree, invertible operations, replay, history, floating panes, drop zones) is replaced by a small pure planner for one or two side-by-side panes, a resizable divider and a small island that applies the host's layout to stable body cells. Kept from the kit: one settled intent per gesture, the tab strip with manual activation, and content that is not re-created when the layout changes. The loss is stated in the decision.

Mounting a React tree after the whole client plugin roster has loaded, binding slots to hooks and installing stylesheets per module have no subject in a server-rendered UI. A page is one complete response from typed views, regions are area C1's host-side registry, and stylesheets are static embedded files assembled once into one layered file.

The package exists to show the DeepSeek mark and name and to play a whale animation derived from a vendor video. The Go project is not upstream's product and upstream's brand guidelines ask others not to use its official materials in a way that suggests endorsement, so no asset is carried; the product's name and mark are configuration with a neutral default, and the decoration is not built.

Typed targets, registered contributions, capture of the target when the gesture begins, resolution under a timeout with failed contributors left out visibly, and one shared menu are kept. Changed: the registry is a host service, the menu is a fragment the host renders, an item is a request to a declared route instead of a browser callback, and a menu is resolved once per opening.

The single reference dialog with grouped commands, subsequence search, inline recording from physical key positions, clearing and restoring is kept. The list is rendered by the host from area C1's command registry; a kit island merges the device's overrides and records a chord through the first-party script's list, set and reset.

The seven volatile config fields (preference, three font sizes, three font lists) become the preference type theme.Appearance, stored per principal and validated by the schema package with the same ranges (text 10 to 22, code 10 to 16, terminal 10 to 20). The config struct theme.Config keeps one live field, Default, which is what a principal with no stored preference gets.

resolutionTimeoutMs (default 1000, volatile) becomes menu.Config.ResolveTimeout, a live duration with default one second and a minimum of one millisecond, read by the host that now resolves the menu; MaxItems bounds one menu.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep the model, change the carrier. Kept: typed target families, providers registered by the feature that owns the target, plain presentation fields, capture of the target at the gesture, cancellation on dismissal and withdrawal on unload. Changed: resolution runs on the host, and an action's browser callback becomes a request to a declared route, which is where the note's rule that an action must recheck mutable resources is enforced. Not carried: React slot contributions and the hook injected into every slot scope.

Final verdict: keep and extend. One symbol per glyph and weight drawn with a use element, inheriting text colour and tokens and replaceable by a theme, is plain SVG and CSS. The sprite becomes an embedded file referenced by address, which removes the note's two stated consequences (no icon without the theme plugin or inside a frame) and lets file-type, site and artwork symbols be replaced too. The registration checks on replacement markup are kept.

Final verdict: keep. A launch acknowledgement says nothing about the background job, so the card must not show a state dot, an exit code or an empty-output line after it. The Go terminal partial takes the same two facts, Background and Running, and draws the same three cases; area C4 supplies them from the tool call. No job state is derived, as the note decides.

Final verdict: nothing to carry. The rule keeps a floating dock panel reachable by resisting at the viewport edge and springing back. The Go dock has no floating panels: a tab that should sit outside the panel opens in a browser window of its own, which the operating system keeps reachable.

Presentation is no longer a set of slot occupants that another package must replace. The product's name and mark are one configuration value (brand.Config) read by every view through brand.Identity, so a deployment changes its identity by configuration.
The canvas whale decoration is not built: it is vendor brand artwork and not a function of the product, so there is no rendering that needs a Canvas 2D context.

The page title is no longer a build-time variable separate from the brand. The shell's title, the navigation header, the about page and the web manifest all read the same run-time value, brand.Identity.

The limit is that Electron's native menu is not used inside the desktop window. There is no desktop application (DH-ADR-18): the page menu is the only programmable menu a browser tab has, and the browser's own menu stays on elements with no target.

The gap came from two kinds of contribution, plain data and React components, of which only the first could be listed. The Go registry has one kind: an item is data plus a request to a route, so every action is in every resolution.
An open menu is still state of one browser tab and is not written to the session log.
justification: This is deliberate. An open menu is view state that DH-ADR-REACT-1 places in the DOM; it has no meaning after the tab closes, and what a menu item does is recorded by the route it calls. Persisting a menu would add a session event with no reader.

reason: Cascading squeeze, snap and priority matter when several dividers share one axis. The Go dock has at most two panes and one divider, sized by a CSS grid in which each pane has its own minimum and the ratio is clamped between 0.2 and 0.8, so there is no neighbour to cascade into.

Upstream's dock depends on pointer drags that were never tuned for touch. In the Go dock every action (open, close, move, split, merge, focus) has a button, a menu item and a key, and only the divider is dragged; it also moves from the keyboard. The real-browser scenario includes a pass with touch emulation; a real touch device is not covered and that is stated.

The divider is a focusable element with the separator role, its orientation and its three value attributes, moved by arrow keys, Home and End. Split, move and close are commands with keys and menu items. Float does not exist. A lint over the rendered markup checks the roles.

Hashed class names came from CSS Modules. Kit stylesheets are plain CSS: the k- class prefix, the data and ARIA attributes each partial renders, and its component properties are the published contract, pinned by golden files and shown in the gallery.

Pane widths and the collapsed navigation are a host preference per principal, written into the generated stylesheet, so a reload and another tab draw the same widths with no flash. Whether the side panel is open is in the URL. A width stays one value per person, not per session, on purpose.

The centre column is minmax(400px, 1fr) in the grid. When the frame cannot hold a 400 px centre beside the side panel, the panel covers the centre instead of squeezing it, and below 768 px the navigation is a page of its own, not a drawer over a column that reserves nothing.

The risk was two separately animated things, the frame's track and the occupant's slide, owned by two packages. In the Go frame only the grid track has a transition; the panel inside it has none, so they cannot move on different curves, and reduced motion removes the one transition.
When a pane opens or is resized the transcript reflows, and whether the reader's line stays in view depends on the browser's scroll anchoring.
justification: Keeping a reading position across a reflow is a browser feature (scroll anchoring). The server-rendered transcript leaves it enabled, so engines that have it keep the line; this design cannot add it to an engine that lacks it without a scroll script in the transcript, which belongs to areas C3 and C4 if they find it necessary.

reason: The managed transfer (an application token plus a Chromium-only DownloadURL, with native delivery left to the desktop application) is not built. Every image shown is served by the host from its own origin, so a download action and the lightbox's link to the original work in every browser; dragging an image out is whatever the browser does natively.
A diff is still bounded and falls back to a coarse whole replacement beyond the bound.
justification: An unbounded diff of model-controlled text is a denial of service. DH-ADR-DIFF-1 keeps a bound but makes it a rule of the two texts alone (bytes and lines), computed once on the host under an input cap, so the same edit always renders the same way and the browser allocates nothing. The coarse result is flagged and shown as such by the diff partial.

reason: Only a fixed list of hosts gets its own mark; every other link keeps the generic glyph.
justification: Recognising an arbitrary site means fetching its icon, which tells that site what the reader is looking at and breaks the rule that nothing leaves the machine unasked (DH-ADR-9). The list is data in the binary and is extended by adding a symbol and a table row.

reason: A reference-style link or footnote whose definition arrives after its block was frozen is shown literally until the reply settles.
justification: Freezing finished blocks is what keeps streaming cost proportional to the reply (DH-ADR-REACT-2, requirement DH-LIB-MICROMARK-R8). Resolving a late definition would mean re-rendering frozen blocks on every chunk. The settled render corrects it, as upstream.

reason: The host appends the lines of an open fence uncoloured and colours the block once, when it closes; a block above a size limit stays plain (DH-LIB-SHIKI requirements R3 and R4). The page therefore never holds token elements for an unbounded fence, and nothing is tokenized in the browser.

The limit came from one copy handler per React Markdown root. Formulas are host-rendered MathML that keeps its TeX source as an annotation (DH-LIB-KATEX requirement R4), and one copy handler wraps the whole transcript, so a selection that spans messages copies TeX. Header controls of a code frame are excluded from selection by CSS. The handler's placement is requested from area C4.

The cost named here is re-tokenizing a streaming diff on every chunk. On the host an open fence is not coloured until it closes, so a diff fence is tokenized once. Colouring each file's sides by the language its header names, and leaving the body plain for an unknown path, are kept as behaviour.
A very long source line is still left uncoloured, and a construct that opens on it can mis-colour the lines after it.
justification: The Go tokenizer's regular-expression engine also backtracks, so the library decision keeps a per-rule time limit and a long-line cut-off (DH-LIB-SHIKI requirement R3). The second half of the upstream limit is gone: highlighting runs on the host and cannot block the page.

reason: The debt is two version-keyed patches whose rule vanishes silently on an upgrade. In Go the rule that a bare URL ends before non-ASCII punctuation is a configured pattern of the Markdown library with its own test (DH-LIB-MICROMARK requirement R5, DH-T-MICROMARK-3); no file is patched. The behaviour itself is kept on purpose.

The patch rewrites one rule of the TextMate Go grammar shipped by the @shikijs/langs npm package when it loads in the browser. The Go design does not use that package: highlighting runs on the host with chroma's own lexers, each rule under a time limit (DH-LIB-SHIKI).

The patch rewrites the match rule of the TextMate Perl grammar from the same npm dependency. The Go design has no TextMate grammars. Whether chroma's Perl lexer mis-colours the same patterns is not known and would be an ordinary defect of DH-LIB-SHIKI, not this patch.
The fish logo is upstream's brand mark and is not carried in any form, so there is no approximation to replace. The Go product draws its own neutral mark as a sprite symbol.

The gap is two atoms with no entry in an external design system. In the Go design the kit is the design source: every partial has registered examples, golden files and a gallery page, and there is no second source it could drift from.

An icon needed a sprite that one plugin put into the main document. The sprite is now an embedded file referenced by address, so any same-origin document, including a framed island, draws icons, and no component has to be loaded first.
The status mark still has five states (done, warning, ongoing, error, idle) and no sixth.
justification: No view in the Go design needs another state: a running agent is ongoing and an open session is marked by selection, not by a dot. The state is a typed constant, so adding one is a token, a CSS rule, an example and a golden file when a consumer asks for it.

reason: The atoms could not reach the locale, so every feature passed complete labels. A Go template can call the catalogue through area C1's helper in the request's language: the kit keeps its standard labels in its own namespace, and a parameter is typed as a message key or as data, so a feature passes a key, not a translated string.
The terminal output frame still replays only line-level control (colours, carriage return, backspace, erase in line, tabs) and strips cursor addressing and screen switches.
justification: Command output is an unbounded stream of lines, while cursor addressing needs a fixed grid with bounded history (libs/micromark.md section 5.4, requirement DH-LIB-ANSER-R2). An interactive program belongs in the terminal island, which is a real emulator.

reason: There is no client roster to wait for. A page is one complete HTTP response, readable before any script runs (requirement DH-LIB-REACT-R1), and a slow region can be a fragment fetched after the page.

Document scopes, Shadow DOM placement and style retention per module are properties of the React renderer that installs plugin stylesheets at run time. The Go UI has no such renderer: stylesheets are static files, and a framed island links the same token stylesheet from its own document.

Suspense and per-entry lazy loading are features of React slot rendering over a client plugin roster. Neither exists in the Go design; an island's module is loaded when its element first appears, by area C1's script.

The draft was invalidated because the dialog re-rendered from a store when the command catalogue changed. In the Go design the held chord lives in the kit island; a composition change refreshes area C1's key table but not the open dialog, and the chord is checked against the current table when it is saved.
A binding is still a physical key position shown with a US-layout key name, browser-reserved chords cannot be bound, and only loaded components contribute rows.
justification: Physical codes are what keep a binding stable across layouts and input methods, and area C1 decides them (DH-ADR-UICORE-6 in areas/ui-core.md). A browser tab cannot take the browser's own chords, and with no desktop application there is no other window. Rows from loaded components only is the intended behaviour of owned lifetimes (DH-O-1).

reason: A theme is registered by a compiled-in component and validated: every token it names must exist, every value must parse as a colour, and an icon replacement must be a well-formed symbol. It is an overlay on the complete built-in values, so it cannot be incomplete; a test checks that every alias has a light and a dark value.

The statement is a governance rule, not a defect: the token file is the only place a colour is defined. The Go design keeps it and enforces it with the stylesheet check, which rejects a literal colour or a static step outside the tokens layer, so a new colour is always a reviewed token with both scheme values.

File-type, site, artwork and brand symbols were inline SVG in components and so could not be replaced. In the Go design every icon family is a symbol in an embedded sprite file, and a registered theme may replace any symbol by id.

The marker asks for a border and a literal shadow to be replaced by the elevation token. In the Go kit an elevated surface must set border 0 and an elevation token, and the stylesheet check rejects a literal colour in a shadow, so the pattern cannot be written.

title: A component is a typed partial: a parameter struct, a named template and a stylesheet
Plain CSS in cascade layers, three tiers of tokens, both schemes in one value, rules enforced by a check
Native elements first, a closed list of kit islands second, and a stated browser floor
The dock is one or two panes with a divider, planned on the host; no floating panels, no nested splits, no drag-to-dock
A context menu is resolved by the host from registered contributions, and an item is a request to a declared route
Every icon is a symbol in an embedded sprite file, referenced by address
No upstream brand asset is carried; the product's identity is configuration with a neutral default
Appearance is a host preference per principal, drawn by an attribute and one generated stylesheet
Every page is built from one library of typed partials
One stylesheet with tokens, layers and scales, and a check that keeps it honest
A person chooses light or dark, text sizes and fonts, and the first paint already shows the choice
Dialogs, menus, tabs, tooltips and pick lists work from the keyboard and are announced correctly
The page's regions keep a readable centre at every width, and a pane width survives a reload
The side panel holds tabs in one or two panes, and moving a tab never restarts its content
A right-click or the menu key shows the actions every loaded feature offers for that thing
A person can look up every shortcut and change one on their device
Icons come from recorded sprite files, and the product shows its own name and mark
A gallery page and golden files show and pin every partial
Every registered example of every partial renders to its golden file in English and Chinese
Validate refuses an unnamed control, an unknown variant and two actions, and a refused struct writes nothing
Hostile strings through every text, id and address field of every partial yield no new markup
Accessibility lint over all golden files: names, roles, references, focusable ids
The stylesheet check rejects each broken rule: literal colours, hover, radius, borders with elevation, prefixes
Every token is defined in both schemes and declared pairs meet their contrast ratio
The assembled stylesheet starts with the layer statement, is deterministic and names no other origin
Every kit island is in the island table and manifest, under its byte limit, with complete fallback children
Appearance validation and the generated stylesheet: ranges, hostile font lists, entity tag
The scheme attribute and head contributions for each preference, with defaults and per-principal isolation
An invalid theme fails registration, and unloading a theme restores the built-in values
The frame preference clamps widths and the frame markup has its landmarks, dividers and collapse control
Property test of the dock planner: two panes at most, no empty pane, stale or invalid intents change nothing
Dock golden files: strip roles, one cell per tab, blocked split with a reason, every intent as a plain form
Menu registry: order, duplicates, a failing or slow contribution omitted and named, unload, access filtering
Menu routes: unknown kind, refusal before resolution, every item names a declared route, roles in the golden file
The shortcut help lists every registered command once with its default chord and no edit control on fixed ones
Icons exist in recorded sprites, and no embedded asset or text matches the brand deny-list
Title, navigation header and identity follow brand configuration, with neutral defaults
Every kit view has an example in the gallery, the gallery exists only when mounted, and kit text is complete in both languages
The terminal partial draws no job state for a background call after its acknowledgement
The widgets are operable by keyboard alone and expose the right roles
The chosen appearance is in the first paint, in both schemes, with no violation
Panes resize and tabs move without restarting content
A context menu shows what is allowed, and a shortcut can be looked up and changed
The required browser features and the widget contract hold in Firefox and Safari
